newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-BECKER EARNS $681,250 FOR ROUTINE DAY.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-BECKER EARNS $681,250 FOR ROUTINE DAY.

text.p: Australian Open champion Boris Becker completed a routine day's work on a tennis court on Thursday and drove home with the guarantee of a $681,250 Christmas bonus.
The three-times Wimbledon champion took just 58 minutes to defeat Swiss Jakob Hlasek 6-4 6-1 in the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam Cup, the richest tournament in the game.

Becker, who lives just a short drive from Munich's Olympic arena, earned $250,000 for just turning up at the event since he has won one of the four grand slams this year. The best performers from Wimbledon and the French, U.S. and Australian Opens qualify for the $6 million event.
A place in the semifinals was worth an extra $431,250 to the German hero. He is still in the running to take home $1.875 million if he wins the tournament.

Becker's wife Barbara, his friends and big names from the world of soccer were in the arena to watch the most famous figure in the German game. Many of the crowd carried large banners. They witnessed a largely uninteresting encounter, however.

Hlasek, who ironically announced his retirement shortly before the tournament, was only called up as a last-minute replacement. The Swiss struggled with his serve throughout the match and put up little opposition to Becker who served and volleyed with punch, precision and pace.
Becker, who lost a dramatic five-set final to Pete Sampras in last month's ATP world championship, said he was playing some of the best tennis of his career at the moment.
"I am on a good track right now. Unfortunately the year has to finish," he said. "It would be nice if I could play Wimbledon next week."
Hlasek's brief comeback, which included a first-round victory over Frenchman Cedric Pioline, has been worth $262,500 to the Swiss.
Hlasek, who has not beaten Becker since their first meeting in 1984 in the Swiss city of Basle when the German was a teenager, struggled with his serve as early as the third game.
Becker eventually broke in the fifth game when Hlasek hit a backhand out of a court after a long rally when the German had the Swiss scurrying about court. He clinched the set after 39 minutes.
After that the match ceased to be a contest. Hlasek was presented with a bunch of flowers at the end to mark his final retirement. It was the only gift he got all day.
Becker said he would be missed on the circuit.
"He is a nice guy. But everyone has to know when to stop. I remember the match in 1984. I got a wild card and I was playing against the local hero as a 16-year-old...I got him back (for the defeat)."
